novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new measurement/application—“a Subliminal Gradient Audit (SGA)” that detects an “anomalously consistent” low-dimensional gradient subspace without knowing the trait—alongside the prediction that “surface-form-preserving transformations ... selectively destroy the subliminal channel.” Searches using “subliminal learning gradient alignment detection audit,” “hidden trait transfer gradient fingerprint,” and “subliminal learning paraphrasing transformation defense” identify the closest work as “Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning: When and How Hidden Biases Transfer” (2025), which already attributes transfer to a small set of divergence tokens and reports that prompt paraphrasing usually suppresses it; thus, the transformation result is largely a direct transfer, while turning known gradient alignment into a trait-agnostic PCA-style dataset detector is a non-trivial but natural operational extension rather than a new core mechanistic relationship. No located work is essentially equivalent to the proactive audit itself, so the combined idea has standard novelty, but its main ingredients—gradient concentration, anomaly detection, and surface-form fragility—are already established or predictable from close prior work.
